items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: Freddie Green was pretty special. I mean you’ve giving a hundred percent all the time, I mean never solo. And why do you think Freddie Green never soloed, because his strings were up so damn — pardon me — so high.

ctx.x: You have to take a certain pride in providing that correctly, that Freddie Green thing. I mean maybe I’m stating the obvious but I don’t think all guitar players can be content with doing that.

Yeah, well it’s — most don’t. It is, it’s a very limiting role. If that’s all I did I’d get, I’d probably go nuts too. Freddie Green was pretty special. I mean you’ve giving a hundred percent all the time, I mean never solo. And why do you think Freddie Green never soloed, because his strings were up so damn — pardon me — so high. You know and basically if those strings are up really high and he had really heavy gauge, thick, heavy strings, with the bridge set so that they’re very high above the fingerboard so…
Wow. He must have had a strong left hand I guess.
